newsitem.title: ITALY: Andreotti accuser discloses his salary as turncoat.
newsitem.headline: Andreotti accuser discloses his salary as turncoat.

text.p: Balduccio Di Maggio, the turncoat who has accused former Italian prime minister Giulio Andreotti of kissing the Mafia's "boss of bosses", said on Friday he had received $328,000 from the state in official money since turning state's evidence.
Di Maggio, testifying at Andreotti's trial on Mafia charges, told the court the state had paid him 500 million lire so far for his participation in a witness protection programme.
Andreotti, who was prime minister seven times and denies accusations he was the Mafia's political protector in Rome, said the payment had been out of line.
"It makes me bitter that the state has given half a billion lire to a slanderer. It does not seem right to me," Andreotti told reporters.

His defence lawyer, Odoardo Ascari, said he was shocked that such a huge sum "was given to a man who dissolved many of his victims in acid", adding that the money "should have gone to victims' families".
Di Maggio told the same court on Thursday that Mafia "boss of bosses" Salvatore Riina kissed Andreotti on both cheeks in a meeting in Palermo in 1987.
Di Maggio was Riina's bodyguard and driver. His decision to co-operate with investigators after his arrest was instrumental to Riina's capture.
Andreotti said the payment would have been justified had it been a reward for information leading to the arrest of Riina, who was captured in 1993 after 23 years at large.
"I'd like to know if he is still receiving a salary but he (Di Maggio) refused to answer that question," said Andreotti, who denies ever meeting Riina.
Di Maggio, who has spoken of the alleged meeting with Riina several times before, has previously described the purported embrace as a mafioso "kiss of honour".
"I know that Andreotti has denied this episode (the kiss) ever took place, but this is the truth," he said on Thursday.
Andreotti's trial, usually held in Palermo, was moved to Rome for security reasons so that Di Maggio could testify.

Andreotti is also on trial in the central city of Perugia charged with complicity in the murder of a journalist, who was planning to expose the financing of his faction of the now-defunct Christian Democrat party.
He denies those charges as well. ($1=1,525 lire)
